## Natural history notes

A small pyralid moth characterized by tan to brown forewings with a distinct darker crossband, fine mottling, and a narrow, triangular resting posture. In Florida, it has been recorded as part of the state’s moth fauna and is likely found in warm wooded, shrubby, or semi-open habitats where adults may come to lights. The caterpillar host information appears limited, though lemon has been listed as one host plant, so it is best treated cautiously as a small nocturnal plant-feeding moth whose larvae feed on foliage and whose adults and larvae support birds, bats, spiders, and parasitoid wasps.
